newsitem.title: USA: BTG has Q4 shr loss, lending term problems.
newsitem.headline: BTG has Q4 shr loss, lending term problems.

text.p: BTG Inc, an information technology services company, said Monday it posted a loss of $0.05 per share in the fourth quarter of its fiscal year 1996 ended March 31.

BTG president and chief executive officer Edward Bersoff said the first nine months of the fiscal year were exceptional, but fourth quarter results were affected by unanticipated events such as cost pressures associated with BTG's rapid expansion and preparation for future growth.

Other reasons for the fourth-quarter results, he said, were increased staffing required to support new government contracts, higher costs of investment in current projects such as Community Networks Inc.

In addition, there were a series of one-time charges, including higher-than-anticipated costs of the consolidation of BTG's Washington-area facilities, a client's bankruptcy, and an increase in certain reserves associated with other commercial business, he said.

Bersoff said significant income was anticipated from shipment of a large order of software products, but the government customer was unable to assemble funding on schedule. He said BTG decided to release this information after receiving word from the customer late Thursday, May 1, that the funding was not available.

BTG's fourth quarter revenue will be about $90 million, compared with $59.8 million in the year-ago quarter and earnings per share are expected to result in a loss of $0.05 against $0.11 earnings per share for the comparable quarter in fiscal 1996, he said.

Due to these results, the company is out of compliance with certain fiscal year 1997 year-end financial covenants under its existing loan agreements, he said. Management expects to obtain waivers from its lenders.

Bersoff said for the 1996 fiscal year, the company expects to report annual revenue of approximately $400 million, up 87 percent from $213.6 million for the previous fiscal year; net income of $4.2 million, up 42 percent more from $3.0 million; and earnings per share of $0.59, up 26 percent from $0.47.
Audited financial results are expected to be released in in mid-May, the company said.
